cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Win the Smaller Concession
cards.instruction: Get one small surrender, then use its logic to make the larger claim harder to defend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sort this windowsill. Can my little basil plant stay in the sunny corner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One little pot. I need room to open the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep the handle clear. If basil can have sun, the parsley beside it will need some too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put both in one trough and do the watering. You still get your handle, and neither herb has to die in the hall.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes charge of arranging sill, A3 accepts the handle condition and uses admitted sunlight need to push for parsley, A5 adds shared care and one-container compromise.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 access limit prompts A3 clear handle; B4 pot count causes A5 joint trough proposal.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants a usable window and B4 enforces the explicit small concession.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses the one-pot wording and equal need for sun to make the broader exclusion harder to defend while maintaining B access.

specificity.evidence: A1 basil/sunny corner and B2 handle establish a concrete domestic arrangement.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 watering and handle assurance pursue permission; dying-in-hall exaggeration presses the plant-care logic.
